top.title: Several soldiers feared dead in Yobe road crash
top.description: By Maryam Abdul-aziz Usman Several soldiers are feared dead, while others sustained injuries in a road accident involving a military vehicle at Garin Malam Adamu, near Buni Yadi, headquarters of Gujba Local Government Area of Yobe State. The accident reportedly occurred on Friday, November 20, while the soldiers were travelling from Buni Yadi to Damaturu, the state capital. The victims were reportedly evacuated to the Yobe State University Teaching Hospital, Damaturu, for medical attention. Although the exact casualty figure remains unknown, preliminary accounts have linked the accident to the poor condition of the affected section of the road. As of the time of filing this report, military authorities had yet to officially confirm the incident or disclose the number of casualties. top.title: 3 Falcons defenders hit with 4 fines from Week 10 loss to Chiefs
top.description: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images | Getty Images The Falcons racked up nine penalties in last week’s lackluster loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, but they were all procedural — there weren’t any flags for actions that typically lead to fines. But that didn’t stop the NFL from issuing four fines total to three different defensive players stemming from last Sunday’s action. Defensive lineman Brandon Dorlus was the lucky guy who got hit with two fines, each for $7,114. One was for unsportsmanlike conduct/taunting, and one was for a late hit on a quarterback. DeMarcco Hellams, who slid into the starting spot opened up by the Falcons’ decision to trade Jessie Bates III to the Jaguars before the NFL’s deadline, owes the NFL $6,509 for unnecessary roughness/a hit on a defenseless player, and linebacker Harold Perkins was also fined $5,203 for unnecessary roughness/use of the helmet. The NFL splits the fine money it collects from players between the NFL Foundation to support the health, safety and wellness of athletes at all levels of football and the Professional Athletes Foundation to support NFL Legends in need. The Wallabies ended a four-match losing run thanks to tries from hooker Brandon Paenga-Amosa, prop Taniela Tupou, wing Max Jorgensen and centre Len Ikitau, while fly-half Carter Gordon kicked a late penalty. Wales captain Dewi Lake scored two tries, while full-back Blair Murray also crossed following a superb assist by wing Louis Rees-Zammit. Replacement hooker Ryan Elias grabbed a late try but Australia held on for victory as Wales paid the price for not capitalising on attacking chances. Wales finished fifth in the northern hemisphere section and will play Japan at the Allianz Stadium in Twickenham on Saturday (13:10 GMT). Australia finished third in the southern hemisphere table and play Ireland on Friday (20:10 GMT). Fans flock back to the Principality Stadium After all the hysteria and celebrations to mark a first victory against the All Blacks in 73 years, the attention turned towards whether Wales could back it up against Australia. There was a vibrancy on the streets of Cardiff before the game not seen for a while, which reflected in the crowd. After crowds of 52,425 against Japan and 55,152 against New Zealand, the 66,307 attendance against Australia was the highest of the autumn. The All Blacks win proved instrumental in a surge of tickets sold for a 20:10 GMT kick-off, the latest for a Wales rugby home game at the Principality Stadium. Head coach Steve Tandy made four changes to revert to the side that beat Japan with flanker James Botham the most notable absentee following his player-of-the-match against New Zealand. Botham was expecting the birth of his first child this week but Tandy stated his omission was for rugby reasons with Cardiff colleague Alex Mann replacing him. Fit-again number eight Aaron Wainwright replaced Taine Basham, while lock Ben Carter and wing Josh Adams returned for Adam Beard and Gabriel Hamer-Webb. top.description: .recover cannabis, codeine syrup, others By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Ogun I Area Command, has intercepted and seized contraband goods with a total Duty Paid Value (DPV) of ₦3.52 billion as part of intensified efforts to curb smuggling, protect public health and safeguard the nation’s economy. The seizures, which include 6,037 wraps of cannabis, 20,500 bottles of codeine-containing cough syrup, more than 1.45 million tablets and capsules of various brands, foreign parboiled rice, petroleum products and vehicles, were inspected and paraded by the Comptroller-General of Customs during a visit to the Command. According to a statement issued on Saturday, by the Public Relations Officer of Ogun I Area Command, Assistant Superintendent of Customs Paul Gimba, the total value of the seized items with available valuations stood at **₦3,517,838,700. The statement said the seizures reflected the Command’s sustained efforts to combat smuggling and prevent the circulation of prohibited and potentially harmful products in the country. A breakdown of the intercepted items showed that cannabis accounted for 6,037 wraps, valued at ₦1.268 billion, while 20,500 bottles of cough syrup containing codeine had a Duty Paid Value of ₦147.6 million. top.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 13: Sidney Crosby #87 of the Pittsburgh Penguins looks on against the Chicago Blackhawks during the first period at United Center on October 13, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. The door is now officially open in Pittsburgh. Kyle Dubas sent a very clear message Wednesday: the Penguins are ready to make moves. With a 7-11-2 record and the team sitting near the bottom of the Eastern Conference standings, the general manager has announced a fire sale. He wants trades focused on the future, bringing in young players who can contribute to the next version of the Penguins. And in the middle of all this, there’s obviously Sidney Crosby. The captain is set to become an unrestricted free agent on July 1. If Pittsburgh decides to move him before then, Crosby himself would have to agree to a trade to a contender. Dubas acknowledged that he had spoken with his veteran players about the organization’s situation and what could happen over the coming weeks. He also emphasized his tremendous respect for Crosby and said he would respect whatever decision the captain makes. In a nutshell, Pittsburgh will trade him to whichever team he wants. In an article published in the Toronto Sun, Bruce Garrioch identified the two potential destinations that could battle for the legendary forward: Colorado and Montreal. Sidney Crosby to Avalanche? The idea of bringing the two superstars together in the same uniform would obviously be incredibly appealing. top.title: Four downs from DeWitt football's state semifinal loss to Zeeland West
top.description: CALEDONIA — Here is reaction from the DeWitt football team falling in a Division 3 state semifinal to Zeeland West 42-26 in a matchup of the last two state champions in D3. Player of the game Niko Mongkhoun, Zeeland West: The senior the tone for the Dux with an 80-yard touchdown run on the opening play of the game. Zeeland West never looked back from there and never trailed while advancing to the state final. Moungkhoun ran for 185 yards on 11 carries and recovered a fumble. Key moment DeWitt trailed 22-13 at half and was set to receive the kick to open the second half. Zeeland West recovered a squib kick to open the third quarter. Less than two minutes later the Dux had capped the drive with a touchdown and added a 2-point conversion to take a 30-13 lead. What it means DeWitt closes its season with an 10-3 record and reached the state semifinals for a third straight year. This is the second time in three seasons the Panthers have had their season end with a loss to Zeeland West in the state semifinal. DeWitt dropped to 0-3 against the Dux in the postseason. Zeeland West reaches the Division 3 state final for the second time in three years with the win and will face Harper Woods at Ford Field on Saturday, Nov. 28. Quotable "Momentum swings are big in any game but especially games of this magnitude. That (squib kick) wasn't a great start for us by any means (in the second half) but we made a lot of mistakes today and part of it is because of them and part of it is us not being as disciplined as we needed to be against a team like that on both sides of the ball and with special teams. If you're going to beat a team that doesn't make many mistakes you can't make them yourselves and we made some today for sure." DeWitt coach Rob Zimmerman Contact Brian Calloway at bcalloway@lsj.com. top.title: Chiefs Fans Slam $3 Billion Stadium Design as Clark Hunt Considers Controversial New Fee
top.description: Chiefs Fans Slam New Stadium Getty Kansas City Chiefs fans aren’t happy with the team’s plans for a new $3 billion stadium in Kansas. Many have criticized the dome design, while others are concerned they could soon have to pay more for season tickets. The Chiefs plan to leave Arrowhead Stadium and move into the new 70,000-seat venue in 2031. However, after seeing images of the proposed stadium, some furious fans questioned why the team is replacing Arrowhead’s open-air setting with a dome. Adding to their frustration, Chiefs chairman Clark Hunt confirmed the team is considering personal seat licenses (PSLs), which would require season ticket holders to pay an additional fee just to purchase their seats. Chiefs Fans Criticize New Stadium Design and Proposed Dome View this post on Instagram The planned stadium has already drawn criticism from fans who believe the design looks too similar to other modern NFL venues. Much of the frustration centers on the decision to build a dome rather than another outdoor stadium. “Sweet… looks like every other stadium built in the last ten years. I’m sure a sellout stadium will be so much better than Arrowhead,” one fan wrote on social media. Another supporter commented, “Not a single soul likes this boring, recycled dome stadium.” Others questioned whether the new venue would offer the same experience as Arrowhead, which has been the Chiefs’ home since 1972. “We do not care. Chiefs fans do not want a dome!” one X user posted. Another added, “Just like every other ugly domed stadium. No one is coming to ‘experience’ this as they do at Arrowhead. Generic trash with zero tradition or history.” Some fans also expressed frustration about not having a say in the stadium plans. “Literally nobody asked for this. The people who bought tickets for 50 years and paid for this stadium had no say in this. 90% of us hate it,” one supporter wrote. The Chiefs have not announced changes to the proposed design in response to the criticism. top.title: Weekend Warm-up: Did Bayern Munich do the right thing in signing Jamal Musiala and Alphonso Davies to massive deals?
top.description: (Photo by Marcel Engelbrecht - firo sportphoto/Getty Images) | Getty Images There is an uncomfortable question hanging over Bayern Munich’s recent contract strategy — did the club make the right investments in Jamal Musiala and Alphonso Davies, or did it allow the fear of losing two exceptional talents to dictate financial decisions that could eventually become difficult to justify? Both players received lucrative, long-term extensions in February 2025. At the time, Bayern Munich vie wed them as essential building blocks for the future. Musiala was arguably the most exciting young attacking talent in German football, while Davies remained one of Eur ope’s most sought-after left-backs. Losing either player, particularly on a free transfer, would have been a significant sporting and financial setback. At the time that each signed, it was reported that neither had a serious suito r. But there was another consideration that could not be ignored — neither player had an entirely clean injury history. Bayern Munich was committing enormous money to two footballers whose availability had already become a recurring concern. top.title: Wake Forest Takes Apart Georgia Tech, 50-29
top.description: | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Tony Siracusa, CFB Managing Editor It wasn’t pretty or artistic. While it was a blowout, it certainly was not the same type of route Wake Forest has been delivering of late; it was good enough to get the job done. Wake Forest takes apart Georgia Tech, 50-29, and gets one game closer to a spot in the ACC championship game. Wake Forest Takes Apart Georgia Tech The weather was dark, gloomy, and sometimes wet during the game. The mood on the field matched. The game was chippy from the outset. Before the game, Wake players were headed to gather in their end zone. It just so happened to be at the same time Georgia Tech was coming out of its tunnel. Words were exchanged, but nothing else. The Usual Early Start And then Wake scored early and often, and some of the aesthetic beauty of the game went by the wayside. By the end, penalty flags became the common sight throughout much of the second half. Wake ended the game with 12 penalties for 111 yards. The conference office can count on hearing from Wake head coach Jake Dickert on a few of them. Wake scored on its first drive of the game, which has become the norm lately. Ty Clark III pushed his way up the middle from four yards out for the touchdown, capping a 12-play, 78-yard drive. The drive featured everything that has been Gio Lopez this season. The drive was a mix of completed passes to three different receivers, some of his own runs (both by design and scrambling), and managing the offense. top.description: France have won back-to-back Six Nations titles [Getty Images] Nations Championship France (14) 45 Tries: Guillard, Mauvaka, Gourgues 2, Gailleton, Duguid, Bielle-Biarrey Cons: Gourgues 5 Argentina (10) 17 Tries: Piccardo, Matera Cons: Albornoz 2 Pen: Albornoz France dispatched Argentina in Paris to book their spot against South Africa in the Nations Championship final at Allianz Stadium next Sunday. Knowing pre-game a bonus-point victory at Stade de France would be enough to edge England out of the top spot in the northern hemisphere standings, Les Bleus had to work hard to secure the points required. Lock Mickael Guillard powered over for the opening score, but Justo Piccardo responded for the visitors before Tomas Albornoz nudged them ahead with a penalty. Argentina have not been at their best this November, suffering a heavy defeat by Ireland before narrowly beating Italy. However, as is often the case with the Pumas, the longer they spend together, the more they tend to improve as a campaign progresses. Felipe Contepomi's side brought the first-half physicality needed to trouble France, who turned to their maul late in the first half to score through Peato Mauvaka and reclaim the lead. Fly-half Matthieu Jalibert, who missed the win over the world champions through injury, then expertly sent Kalvin Gourgues through a gap to score. The pivotal moment came when Argentina prop Mayco Vivas was shown a 20-minute red card for making direct head contact at a ruck, with France capitalising on the extra man to score their bonus-point try through Emilien Gailleton. Hooker Julian Montoya then joined Vivas in the sin-bin after receiving a yellow card and France made their numerical advantage count once again as Tyler Duguid and Gourgues crossed. Pablo Matera intercepted Louis Bielle-Biarrey's pass to improve the scoreline but Bielle-Biarrey made amends to dot down a brilliant kick into space by Antoine Dupont. It will now be rematch of last Friday's epic game in Paris, which France narrowly won 21-19 against the world champions. South Africa booked their spot in the final by picking up a losing bonus point against Ireland. Scotland will play Argentina on Sunday at Allianz Stadium in the seventh/eight-place play-off. nigeria.description: A survivor of Friday’s boat accident in the Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has recounted how she struggled to escape from the capsized vessel, saying she lost several members of her family and neighbours in the tragedy. The woman, whose identity was not immediately disclosed, said her elder sister, her sister’s daughter-in-law and two children belonging to her relatives and neighbours were among those who died in the accident. Recounting the incident, she said the boat suddenly capsized, trapping passengers beneath it. “The boat just fell and pressed all of us. My elder sister’s son’s wife was lost. My elder sister was lost. Her son was also lost. One of my neighbours who followed us also lost her son. My neighbour herself was lost,” she said. ﻿ The survivor said she was the only person among those close to her who made it out alive, adding that she struggled to escape after the boat overturned. “It’s only me that is safe. When I came out, somebody held me. I was drinking water. I was not able to come out. I struggled before I came out. Where we were standing, the boat broke from above and pressed us down,” she said. Asked by the Bayelsa governor, Douye Diri, whether the bodies of her missing relatives and neighbours had been recovered, she replied in the negative. Her account comes as the death toll from the accident has risen to 23, while 24 survivors are receiving treatment in hospitals. nigeria.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Veteran actor Richard Mofe-Damijo, popularly known as RMD, has opened up about the emotional challenges of losing loved ones, describing grief as one of the hardest experiences he has had to deal with. nigeria.title: Alcaraz to face Zverev for ATP Finals title
nigeria.description: Carlos Alcaraz rallied past Ben Shelton on Saturday to book his spot in the ATP Finals title match, where he will meet world number one Alexander Zverev as he bids to lift the trophy for the first time. The 23-year-old quickly fell behind 3-0 and was unable to claw his way back into the set. In the second frame, Alcaraz upped his level, gaining the upper hand by breaking to lead 5-3 before levelling at one set all. nigeria.title: Tinubu doing fantastic job on sports infrastructure, says Infantino
nigeria.description: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has commended President Bola Tinubu’s administration for its investment in sports infrastructure, describing its efforts as a “fantastic job” and an indication of Nigeria’s commitment to the future of its young population. Infantino gave the commendation on Saturday while addressing the 48th Ordinary General Assembly of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) in Abuja. The FIFA president urged members of the Nigerian delegation to convey his regards to Tinubu, while acknowledging the contributions of the President and other Nigerian leaders to sports development. “On behalf of President Tinubu, please send him our warmest regards. He is doing together with all of you. Fantastic job here in Nigeria, showing that you are a country projected into the future,” Infantino said. He particularly praised investments in sports facilities, noting that they reflected confidence in the potential of young Nigerians. “We were discussing this yesterday as well, also with the Chairman of the National Sports Commission, my brother Shehu. The investments done in sports facilities infrastructure show that you believe in your youth, in the young girls and the young boys of Nigeria,” he said. “Thank you for that. Congratulations for that,” he added. Infantino also thanked Nigeria for hosting him and his delegation, which included FIFA Secretary-General Mattias Grafström, describing the visit as an opportunity to reconnect with the continent. “Thanks for welcoming me and our delegation with the Secretary-General and the others here at home in Africa, in Abuja. Thank you for your support. It means the world to me,” he said. His remarks followed an inspection of sports infrastructure projects in Nigeria on Friday, including the remodelled Warri City Stadium and the Hussey College mini-stadium and sports complex in Delta State. He also visited the ongoing FIFA Forward Technical Centre project at the Moshood Abiola National Stadium in Abuja, describing the facility as an investment in the future of Nigerian football. “This is a collaboration between Nigerian football and FIFA for the future of the girls and the boys of Nigeria,” he said. During his visit to the Warri City Stadium, Infantino stressed the importance of developing grassroots sports facilities to ensure that football remained accessible to people across communities. “That’s what football is about. It’s for everyone, everywhere. It’s the big stadiums, it’s the World Cup, but it’s also the smaller stadiums, it’s the proximity,” he said. The FIFA president also expressed appreciation for the reception he received in Nigeria, assuring the country of the world football governing body’s continued support. “I feel so much the love of Africa, the love of Nigeria. nigeria.title: Arsenal held by Newcastle rally and lose Raya to injury
nigeria.description: Arsenal missed the chance to open up an eight-point lead at the top of the Premier League after a stirring second-half fightback from Newcastle held the defending champions to a 2-2 draw on Saturday. The Gunners led through Eberechi Eze’s strike after a dominant first 45 minutes. But Mikel Arteta’s men were suddenly headed for defeat when goals from Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw provided a much-needed boost for under-fire Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle. Noni Madueke salvaged a point for Arsenal and stretched their lead at the top over surprise package Brighton to six points. However, the loss of influential goalkeeper David Raya to injury could provide a twist in the title race that many believed Arsenal would cruise. Newcastle remain in the bottom half of the table with just one win in six games in all competitions. Yet, Jaissle can point to his side’s second half performance as a potential turning point after a difficult start to his reign at St. James’ Park. Arsenal move back six points clear of third-placed Manchester City, but missed the chance to put their foot down in the defence of their title. Madueke continued his impressive form in the injury absence of Bukayo Saka and hit the post early on. Former Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes was roundly booed on his first return to Tyneside since making a £75 million ($98 million) move to the Emirates Stadium In August. The Brazilian nearly silenced his former faithful when he prodded just wide from a Madueke cross as Arsenal pressed for the opener. It duly arrived 10 minutes before the break when Kai Havertz pounced on a poor touch by Lewis Hall and brilliantly played in Eze to blast high past Lukas Hornicek. Jaissle got the response he needed from his half-time team talk as Newcastle came out a completely different proposition after the break. Arsenal also played a part in letting the home side back into the game and lifting the 50,000 crowd in doing so. Martin Odegaard shanked his attempt at a long ball forward to allow William Osula to play in Barnes to level. Suddenly an Arsenal side that had kept seven clean sheets in their opening 10 league games was on the rocks. Thiaw bundled home a second for Newcastle just 13 minutes later after Dan Burn was left completely unmarked from a corner and his header was only parried by Raya. That proved to be one of Raya’s final interventions as the Spaniard had to be replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga. Raya would be a massive miss if the Spaniard is sidelined for a significant spell. But Arsenal regained their composure in time to salvage a point that keeps them well in the driving seat to retain the title. Odegaard made amends for his earlier error by freeing Madueke down the right and he cut inside before his tame deflected shot found a way past Hornicek. nigeria.title: 2027 Election: INEC failed on voters’ register – ADC
nigeria.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The African Democratic Congress, ADC, has described the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC’s decision to postpone the clean-up of the national voters’ register until after the 2027 general elections as a major failure. The party said INEC had four years to prepare for the exercise. However, ADC said the voters’ register is only one of several issues that will determine the credibility of the 2027 elections. They pointed to electronic transmission of results, result collation and compliance with the Electoral Act as other major areas of concern. Speaking to Vanguard, the ADC National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, said INEC’s failure to clean up the register raised questions about its commitment to conducting credible elections. “This shouldn’t have happened. INEC had four years to prepare and plan for this, and its failure to do so does not suggest that it is taking its responsibilities seriously, particularly the issue of maintaining a credible voters’ register,” he said. Abdullahi, however, said the party would not make the outcome of the 2027 elections depend solely on whether INEC produced a credible voters’ register, noting that previous elections had been conducted despite imperfections in the register. “We do not believe that the credibility of the 2027 general election rests solely on INEC’s ability to produce a credible voters’ register. It would have given everyone greater confidence if the commission had been able to do so, but we are not going to hinge the fate of the 2027 election on that single issue.” He said the ADC was also concerned about how INEC would implement the Electoral Act, particularly the electronic transmission of results from polling units, the collation process and the duties of electoral officers regarding Forms EC8A and EC8E. “There are other, more pertinent issues of concern to our party. These include compliance with the Electoral Act, the electronic transmission of results from polling units, the collation of results and the additional responsibilities assigned to electoral officers regarding Forms EC8A and EC8E.” On the possible effect of the voters’ register on the elections, Abdullahi argued that strict compliance with the law, particularly provisions on voter accreditation, could reduce the impact of its shortcomings. “If INEC complies with the Electoral Act, particularly regarding voter accreditation, the shortcomings in the voters’ register may not have as much impact. Problems arise when the commission fails to abide by its own rules and the provisions of the Electoral Act,” he said. business.title: SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme The Securities and Exchange Commission has frozen the assets of Indianapolis-based Backward Hat Capital and its two co-founders, saying the firm ran a $560 million Ponzi scheme that told investors their money would be turned into crypto and used for AI-driven currency trading. The agency said Backward Hat, co-founders Phillip Williams and Devin Johnson, Johnson’s firm Traders Point Capital and Joseph Anderson raised the money from more than 2,000 investors starting in July 2022. A federal court granted a temporary restraining order, an asset freeze and expedited discovery to halt what the SEC called an ongoing scheme. Federal prosecutors in New York and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission brought parallel cases. The SEC and CFTC suits were filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Indiana, and the CFTC said the court has appointed Kevin B. Duff as temporary receiver to take control of the companies and the individual defendants’ assets. The pitch: crypto, AI and 6% a month According to the SEC’s complaint , Williams and Johnson sold limited partnership interests in private funds through a network of promoters, including to Williams’s former investment advisory clients. They promised a proprietary, “AI-driven” algorithm that supposedly returned at least 6% every month by trading foreign exchange. Investor money, the pitch went, would first be converted into a crypto asset and then used for that arbitrage. The complaint does not name bitcoin as the asset. It says about $109 million of the roughly $210 million raised from July 2022 to September 2025 was sent to the fund’s Coinbase account and converted. Of that, more than $56 million went to personal crypto accounts held by Williams, Johnson and a relief defendant, according to the complaint. About $40 million ended up on three platforms where some of it was used to trade other crypto assets, but little to no money was used to trade FX. After October 2025, the scheme raised about $350 million, and none of it was sent to Coinbase. Where the money went The SEC said the defendants made more than $250 million in Ponzi payments to earlier investors and moved more than $220 million to themselves. The money paid for exotic cars, expensive homes, private air travel and other businesses they owned, and helped feed Johnson’s gambling. Promoters took more than $50 million. Anderson is accused of producing fake financial reports, including at least two “audit reports” and a “quality of earnings” report from a supposedly independent firm. The SEC said the documents falsely claimed the returns had been verified against bank and brokerage records. It said Anderson did no audit work, was not independent and had a financial stake in the scheme. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. We had reconnected after a long time and started seeing each other more often, especially after I resumed work following an accident I was involved in. He gradually became part of my daily routine. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. Beyond the guilt, there was another question I couldn’t get out of my head: Why did God allow us to reconnect? Why, after such a long time, did our paths have to cross again? entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. Beyond efficiency, integrated platforms may also create new opportunities for financial institutions to deepen SME relationships by using richer payments and business-management data to better understand cash flow patterns, support risk assessment, and potentially enable more relevant lending solutions over time. entertainment.description: Tems receiving the Best African Music Performance at the 67th Annual Grammy Awards. In June 2023, ahead of the 66th Grammy Awards, the Recording Academy announced the creation of the Best African Music Performance category. Its creation was a recognition of how far African music had travelled globally, and Nigerian artists were at the centre of that movement. From Burna Boy ‘s Ye , CKay ‘s Love Nwantiti , Wizkid ‘s explosive Essence , to Rema ‘s globally successful Calm Down and others, Nigerian artists became drivers of African music’s global expansion. Afrobeats – the umbrella term often used internationally to describe much of contemporary African popular music, although many Nigerian artists have rejected it for its tendency to limit the range of music coming out of the country – became an established genre globally. While Nigerian and African music have always travelled beyond their respective countries, the era of streaming and digital platforms has accelerated how quickly global audiences discover and engage with the music. African music became increasingly established in the West and other parts of the world, creating greater recognition for its artists and sounds. The Grammys’ decision to introduce a category specifically recognising African music performances was an important step in that direction, beyond the recognition African artists had previously received in categories such as Best Global Music Album. Although the creation of the Best African Music Performance category was celebrated throughout the continent, there seems to be a monopoly, or something close to it, of Nigerian music in the category. While South African artist Tyla has won the award twice, more than any individual Nigerian artist, Nigerian artists have consistently enjoyed greater representation in the nominations. Indeed, Nigerian artists are considerably more recognised globally, particularly in the West. However, I believe it is the responsibility of an award of this repute to look beyond the most visible names and recognise the best African music released within its eligibility period. A song should not earn a nomination simply because it is popular or has enjoyed international success. In 2026, three of the five recordings featured Nigerian artists, while the 2027 nominations saw four out of five recordings feature at least one Nigerian artist. After crowds of 52,425 against Japan and 55,152 against New Zealand, the 66,307 attendance against Australia was the highest of the autumn. Fit-again number eight Aaron Wainwright replaced Taine Basham, while lock Ben Carter and wing Josh Adams returned for Adam Beard and Gabriel Hamer-Webb. sports.title: Four downs from DeWitt football's state semifinal loss to Zeeland West
sports.description: CALEDONIA — Here is reaction from the DeWitt football team falling in a Division 3 state semifinal to Zeeland West 42-26 in a matchup of the last two state champions in D3. Player of the game Niko Mongkhoun, Zeeland West: The senior the tone for the Dux with an 80-yard touchdown run on the opening play of the game. Zeeland West never looked back from there and never trailed while advancing to the state final. Moungkhoun ran for 185 yards on 11 carries and recovered a fumble. Key moment DeWitt trailed 22-13 at half and was set to receive the kick to open the second half. Zeeland West recovered a squib kick to open the third quarter. Less than two minutes later the Dux had capped the drive with a touchdown and added a 2-point conversion to take a 30-13 lead. What it means DeWitt closes its season with an 10-3 record and reached the state semifinals for a third straight year. This is the second time in three seasons the Panthers have had their season end with a loss to Zeeland West in the state semifinal. DeWitt dropped to 0-3 against the Dux in the postseason. Zeeland West reaches the Division 3 state final for the second time in three years with the win and will face Harper Woods at Ford Field on Saturday, Nov. 28. Quotable "Momentum swings are big in any game but especially games of this magnitude. That (squib kick) wasn't a great start for us by any means (in the second half) but we made a lot of mistakes today and part of it is because of them and part of it is us not being as disciplined as we needed to be against a team like that on both sides of the ball and with special teams. The Usual Early Start And then Wake scored early and often, and some of the aesthetic beauty of the game went by the wayside. sports.title: Why the Alamodome's real NFL legacy endures in cities other than San Antonio
sports.description: The Alamodome is seen with the San Antonio skyline on Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026, from the city's East Side neighborhood. (Andrew J. Whitaker/San Antonio Express-News) Through the bus window, a young NBA player saw something that caught his attention. And as the Golden State Warriors rolled past downtown San Antonio on their way to Frost Bank Center, he asked a longtime member of the team's traveling party an obvious question. "Why is there a football stadium here?" the player wondered. That was two Fridays ago, and it was far from the first time in its 33-year history that the Alamodome's mere existence has served as a source of consternation. On that Warriors bus, for instance, not even those who'd been coming here for decades were sure they understood the building's intended purpose. Had they stayed through the weekend and secured a local newspaper, they might have learned a thing or two. Last Sunday, a front-page story by Express-News reporter Madison Iszler provided an in-depth look at the dome's uncertain future, which won't include another significant overhaul until at least 2035, when demolition might be one of the options on the table. The Alamodome never became the permanent home of an NFL franchise, despite the unrealistic dreams of the officials and voters who approved its construction. It eventually became obsolete, not only by the standards of the world's richest sports league, but also by those of the College Football Playoff and men's basketball Final Fours now spurning it to set up shop elsewhere. Let it not be said, however, that the Alamodome lacks a real NFL legacy. In its own way, it reshaped the geography of professional football. And across this country there are more than a couple of billionaires who owe the odd-looking structure on Montana Street a debt of gratitude, not to mention a chunk of their wealth. After all, nobody loved the Alamodome more than the owners who used it as a threat. Look around the NFL today. More than 12% of its franchises play in palaces funded at least in part by public money that was approved amid rumblings that San Antonio might be willing and able to steal those teams away. The Arizona Cardinals play in State Farm Stadium, which was built with the help of $455 million provided by Maricopa County voters in 2001 . The New Orleans Saints play in the Caesars Superdome, which was renovated after 2005's Hurricane Katrina with the help of a $41 million bond package . The Minnesota Vikings play in U.S. Bank Stadium, which was built with a combined $500 million in state and city funds approved by the Minnesota legislature and Minneapolis city government in 2012. And the Las Vegas Raiders play in Allegiant Stadium, built after the Nevada legislature approved a plan in 2016 to use $750 million in public money. In each of those cities, there had been media reports that the teams were considering a move to San Antonio, where a 64,000-seat dome was sitting empty. Some of the flirting was overt. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
science.description: null On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule. Rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible. Danish astronomer Ole Rømer (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons) Why it mattered Understanding that the speed of light is a constant is the key that opened our ability to gauge the scale of the universe, as well as was central to developing modern physics. "The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so."

Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

Following the sad news of Sir Patrick Stewart's passing , there's been no shortage of discussion about his best moments as Captain Jean-Luc Picard . "The Inner Light"'s life in 25 minutes is a strong contender, as are the courtroom grandstanding in "The Measure of a Man" and his insistence (under extreme torture) that "there are four lights!" in "Chain of Command". But for this writer's money, it's hard to look past a nine-minute sequence in "Star Trek: First Contact", which turns 30 this weekend. With the Borg overrunning the newly launched USS Enterprise-E, Picard — who has long-standing beef with the Collective, following his assimilation in classic "The Next Generation" story " The Best of Both Worlds " — orders his crew to fight the cybernetic nasties hand-to-hand if required, defying their pleas to activate the ship's self-destruct system and retreat. He even calls Worf — not a man renowned for dodging a fight — a coward, prompting the Klingon to respond that, "If you were any other man, I would kill you where you stand." Ouch. But following some impassioned talk about making the Borg "pay for what they've done", he's finally talked down from his rage by 21st-century stowaway Lily Sloane (Alfre Woodard). She points out that his Moby-Dick-esque obsession is on the verge of going full Ahab, and he eventually sees sense, issuing the order to abandon the Enterprise and destroy the hive. It's a masterclass showcasing the ever-brilliant Stewart's impressive range, as the out-of-control captain's rarely seen temper reaches fever pitch, before normal service is resumed. His subsequent apology to Worf — "As a matter of fact, I think you're the bravest man I've ever known" — is simply perfect. And just as the franchise's zenith, "The Wrath of Khan", is built around Kirk and Khan's decades-old feud, "First Contact" is precision engineered to get the most out of Jean-Luc. This was the right "Star Trek" at the right time, a film that put "TNG"'s greatest villains on a collision course with the origins of Starfleet. science.description: null The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit . He didn't say where Ship would be put on display, but the likeliest locale is Starbase, SpaceX's Starship manufacturing and launch hub. (SpaceX plans to shift most Starship launches to its new Starbase Louisiana site, but construction has yet to begin on that $100 billion complex.) Musk participated virtually in the TomorrowX conversation, which was moderated by two friends of his, the venture capitalists Gavin Baker and Antonio Gracias. (TomorrowX took place in Austin, Texas, but Musk was in China on Wednesday as part of President Trump's delegation for his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.) The world's richest man expounded on Ship 42's historic achievement, explaining that it gets SpaceX much closer to the "holy grail of rocketry" — a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. Before Flight 15, SpaceX had already caught Starship's first-stage booster, known as Super Heavy, on three separate occasions , and it had reflown a booster twice. science.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo probe arrives in orbit around Mercury today
science.description: null Mercury is about to receive a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — will arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. The big moment will come after an orbit-insertion burn, which is scheduled to begin today at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT) and last for 37 minutes. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio. The duo launched — along with a power and propulsion element called the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) — aboard an Ariane 5 rocket from French Guiana in October 2018 , beginning a long and looping trip through the inner solar system. Mercury is a difficult planet to reach because it's so close to the sun . Spacecraft approaching the solar system's innermost planet are accelerated to high velocities by the immense gravitational pull of our star and must shed a great deal of kinetic energy to be captured by Mercury's much weaker tug. So the BepiColombo team designed a trajectory that featured one flyby of Earth , two of Venus and six of Mercury over the course of about seven years. That flight time was increased by a year , however, after the mission suffered an issue with its solar panels, which reduced the power available for the MTM's electric thrusters. BepiColombo's arrival at Mercury will take a total of about six months. (Image credit: European Space Agency) Today's orbital insertion is the latest milestone in BepiColombo's Mercury arrival phase, which is expected to take about six months in total. Arrival began on Sept. 3, when the MTM released MPO and Mio. The two orbiters remain connected today; they won't separate until Dec. 9 or thereabouts. Shortly thereafter, Mio will settle into its final orbit, a highly elliptical path that will take it over Mercury's poles. MPO is also destined for a polar orbit, though a much less elliptical one than Mio's; the ESA probe will conduct a series of engine burns before finally getting there on March 10, 2027. BepiColombo won't start doing science work until April 6, 2027. The two probes will gather complementary data from their two different vantage points, shedding a great deal of light on a mysterious world. "The mission will study all aspects of Mercury, from the structure and dynamics of its magnetosphere and how it interacts with the solar wind , to its internal structure with its large iron core, and the origin of the planet’s magnetic field," ESA officials wrote in a BepiColombo mission description . "The data will enable scientists to understand more about the origin and evolution of a planet located close to its parent star, and a better understanding of the overall evolution of our solar system," they added.

science.title: What is the Riemann hypothesis and why is its solution so monumental?
science.description: Bernhard Riemann set out a problem mathematicians have been trying solve for more than a century The Granger Collection/Alamy The cadence of prime numbers has a pattern; it isn’t simply chaos. Mathematician Bernhard Riemann suspected this was the case, but he never proved it conclusively, and his mathematical successors have spent more than a century trying to demonstrate that he was right. The Riemann hypothesis may now be proven , and it could reveal the most basic structure of our number system, while also opening the door for a new understanding of the vast world of mathematical functions. Read more Mathematicians and AI in behind-the-scenes battle over what’s true In 1859, Riemann made a casual remark about a mathematical function in his memoir, qualifying a statement about it as “very probably” true. The fact that he never proved it more definitively has held the world of mathematics in suspense ever since, and the “Riemann hypothesis” became the field’s most famous and stubbornly unsolved problem – until now. A new AI-assisted proof by Levent Alpöge at Anthropic may have just ended a whole era of mathematics by confirming Riemann’s hunch from nearly 200 years ago. “This result, if true, will be the culmination of a struggle thousands of mathematicians have attempted in the past,” says Christopher Hughes at the University of York in the UK. The proof of the Reimann hypothesis is also one of the Clay Mathematics Institute ’s Millennium Prize Problems, each of which comes with a $1 million prize for a solution. Advertisement The Riemann hypothesis has loomed so large over mathematicians for decades because it concerns mathematics’ most simple yet hard-to-understand objects: prime numbers . These are numbers that aren’t divisible by any number other than 1 and themselves, and any number can be built by multiplying primes. In this way, primes are the bones of all systems of numbers; everything is built on top of them. But how primes are distributed among all numbers is, on the face of it, unpredictable. This is where Riemann made an intervention. He hypothesised that the way primes are spaced throughout the number line can be inferred from another set of numbers, now tied to a mathematical function called the Riemann zeta function. These numbers are complex – so each is actually a pair of numbers, one called real and one called imaginary – and when they are plugged into the Riemann zeta function, the function spits out zero. Confusingly, these numbers that result in a zero from the function are called “non-trivial zeros”. Riemann discovered that summing over a sequence of these complex numbers allowed him to predict the distribution of primes up to a certain high number. Effectively, he came upon a formula that could make sense of primes’ seemingly random appearances among numbers. science.description: null On Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station launched into orbit. The 42,000-pound module is called Zarya, and it's about the size of a tour bus. Zarya launched on board a Russian Proton rocket . Two weeks later, NASA's STS-88 shuttle mission aboard Endeavour brought the Unity module into space. The STS-88 astronauts connected the two modules in orbit. Zarya was built by the Russians, but it was paid for by the United States. The module also has docking ports for Russian Progress cargo ships and Soyuz spacecraft that carry crews to and from the space station. science.title: Don't turn the moon into the Wild West, scientists warn
science.description:
Tereza is a London-based science and technology journalist, aspiring fiction writer and amateur gymnast. Originally from Prague, the Czech Republic, she spent the first seven years of her career working as a reporter, script-writer and presenter for various TV programmes of the Czech Public Service Television. She later took a career break to pursue further education and added a Master's in Science from the International Space University, France, to her Bachelor's in Journalism and Master's in Cultural Anthropology from Prague's Charles University. She worked as a reporter at the Engineering and Technology magazine, freelanced for a range of publications including Live Science, Space.com, Professional Engineering, Via Satellite and Space News and served as a maternity cover science editor at the European Space Agency.

Researchers are calling for a moratorium on industrial exploitation of the moon, fearing that rapid development could cause irreversible environmental damage and destroy invaluable scientific material. Both China and the U.S. are pushing forward with plans to establish permanent human settlements on the moon by the end of the next decade. Commercial players want to build businesses supporting these future explorers by mining for resources such as water , construction materials, industrial metals and rare earth minerals. However, some scientists argue that a temporary ban on lunar industrialization is necessary to allow regulations to catch up and limit what can be allowed in order to prevent a moon rush from destroying the pristine lunar environment. Two such researchers are Florian Rabitz, a professor of climate and technology governance at Vilnius University in Lithuania, and Xiao-Shan Yap, an assistant professor of Earth-space sustainability at Utrecht University in the Netherlands. In a piece published last month in the journal Global Environmental Politics , the pair call for "robust international regulations" and "broad and inclusive deliberation" to allow the global community to carefully consider the impact of economic activities on the moon. In addition to the threat to the scientifically priceless lunar landscape, the researchers also object to the colonization of the moon by a small number of powerful players — namely China, the U.S. and their respective close allies. "With the moon it's absolutely clear that whoever is doing the big infrastructure work is going to be asserting their position, including by defining their own exclusive territories," Rabitz said in a statement . "That shouldn't be the Wild West." Rabitz pointed out that, although the United Nations' 1967 Outer Space Treaty prevents individual nations from appropriating the moon, Earth's natural satellite and its valuable resources are unlikely to remain truly neutral territory if its exploitation is going to be led by a small number of powerful nations.

Selected projects include next-generation battery solutions, robotic systems with sensing capabilities for the extreme lunar environment, and tools to prepare for construction of critical infrastructure, such as lunar landing pads. NASA’s SBIR/STTR program provides support for entrepreneurs, startups, and small businesses to advance and commercialize technologies that can advance the agency’s missions. Working with the program, a company’s path toward commercialization or infusion into NASA missions occurs in phases. The latest awards involved two of these phases. The new Phase I contracts will receive up to $225,000 each to establish the merit and feasibility of their proposed innovation. A portion of the projects selected are STTR awards, provided to small businesses partnered with research institutions. The Phase II awards, with 98 contracts valued at up to $1.3 million each, will continue work begun in Phase I projects selected in 2025, targeting demonstration and delivery of the innovative technologies. Following are a few examples of research supported through these recent awards: Bringing Power to Moon and Mars An SBIR Phase II award for Opterus Research and Development Inc. supports a project focused on bringing power to the surface of the Moon and Mars by developing a modular system of rollable solar arrays. The arrays can be handled robotically, are compatible with various support structures, and work even in dusty surface conditions. The technology could be scaled up to 50 kilowatts, and it could provide a reliable power source to help both NASA and commercial space companies develop infrastructure on the Moon . The firm’s 10-foot, extendable robotic arm can both “see” and has a sense of touch, combining a camera with sensors to detect and measure surface textures, contact forces, and temperature. science.title: GTA hasn't gone to space (yet), but these sci-fi games can offer you a life of crime among the stars
science.description: GTA 6 has only just come out, and it's already taken the world by storm and positioned itself as one of the greatest games of all time . Great news for gamers, but what about sci-fi fans? To this day, Rockstar Games sadly hasn't embraced sci-fi with any of its open-world games (save for those UFO Easter eggs). It doesn't seem likely they'll journey to the stars anytime soon — you can't really do cutting societal satire about space — but that doesn't mean there aren't GTA-adjacent sci-fi adventures set in outer space. The frustrating thing is that no one has exactly cracked that pitch yet. Non-linear games set in outer space tend to be either too ambitious, like No Man's Sky, or too focused on specific experiences like space combat, like Star Wars: Squadrons. The end result is a roster of great sandboxes that let us journey to different star systems, but no game that dares to explore a criminal fantasy with the level of depth and opportunities seen in the last few Rockstar games. With new hardware powering far more complex open-world games, it's only a matter of time before "GTA in space" is a real thing. For now, there are some space games that let us explore sci-fi worlds, roleplaying as criminals and outlaws amongst the stars. Roleplaying a space outlaw (Image credit: Bethesda Softworks) Massive space RPGs like Starfield and The Outer Worlds 2 offer vast playgrounds you can explore and redefine through your actions. The lawful path is the obvious choice if you'd like to save the galaxy, but a life of crime awaits those who tire of the heroics. Starfield even has a "new game plus" mechanic baked into the player's journey, encouraging experimentation and living different lives, so if you stick with the divisive space RPG, the criminal life is all but unavoidable. And in traditional Bethesda fashion, you're not rushed to the next "main" objective, so if you want to become the most dangerous space criminal in the Settled Systems, you'll be supported by the mechanics and systems. You can always get back to saving the galaxy when you feel like it. (Image credit: Xbox Game Studios) The Outer Worlds 2 is another option if you want to become a star-surfing scoundrel. It might not be as absurdly expansive as Starfield, but Obsidian's whole deal has always been freedom of choice and roleplaying, so you can bet this humorous sequel also lets the protagonist become a bit of an a-hole. The main story already sets you in a collision course with corporate interests, too. Like in Mass Effect and other classic space RPGs, it's your choice to be either a goody-two-shoes or an edgy maniac, and I won't lie: the second option is usually more entertaining. Last but not least, there's a third game that also has enough going on to support a GTA-inspired fantasy in outer space: No Man's Sky . science.title: Trouble at Mars: NASA's Perseverance rover, Odyssey orbiter halt science work due to glitches
science.description: null Two of NASA's Mars explorers are sidelined by glitches at the moment. The Perseverance rover and Mars Odyssey orbiter have stood down from science work due to technical problems, NASA announced on Thursday (Nov. 19). Perseverance has been sidelined by an antenna issue, and the venerable Odyssey is dealing with a balky reaction wheel. NASA hopes both can get back to work at Mars by the end of November. Communication issues for Perseverance Perseverance landed inside Mars' Jezero Crater in February 2021, tasked with assessing the area's potential to support past life and with collecting dozens of samples for future return to Earth. It has done all this and more. The Perseverance team has determined that Jezero hosted a potentially habitable lake billions of years ago. And the car-sized rover has found a wealth of complex organic compounds in Martian rock, some of which might themselves be signs of life (though assessing this hypothesis fully will likely require bringing Perseverance's samples to Earth for analysis, scientists stress). In addition, Perseverance just set a new distance record for off-Earth driving, rolling past the mark set by its smaller cousin, NASA's Opportunity rover (28.06 miles, or 45.16 kilometers). Perseverance broke that record on Oct. 11. Just 19 days later, however, the mission team noticed a problem: The rover's main UHF downlink radio — which it uses to send information home to Earth, via data-relay satellites in Mars orbit — failed to send its usual "heartbeat" pings to the main computer. Perseverance detected this problem autonomously and reacted as it was programmed to do: The six-wheeled robot switched to its backup UHF radio and went into a protective "safe mode," shutting down all non-essential systems. The rover team recovered Perseverance from safe mode but soon noticed another issue: "The backup UHF radio was transmitting at about half of its expected power output," NASA officials wrote in an update on Thursday . Perseverance's handlers have stopped using that backup radio as well; the rover is now communicating with Earth directly (without the help of relay orbiters), sending signals to NASA's Deep Space Network dishes via its high-gain antenna. This pathway features lower data rates, and the mission team wants to prioritize the delivery of diagnostic information. So they've paused Perseverance's science work, which includes observations by its various cameras. The glitch may be disappointing to devoted Perseverance fans, many of whom have already noticed that the mission website hasn't uploaded any new raw images since Nov. 7 . But there's no reason to panic, according to NASA. "The rover is stable and communicating with the team," agency officials wrote in Thursday's update. "The team is hopeful the rover could return to science by the end of November, and NASA will provide further updates in the future as the team works the issue." science.title: There's an impostor hiding in the Hyades star cluster. Can you spot it?
science.description: null For years I looked at Taurus and saw something perfectly sensible. There was the Hyades, the big V-shaped cluster that forms the bull's face, with Aldebaran, noticeably brighter and more orange than the other stars, the dominant star. Every diagram reinforced the arrangement — Aldebaran was the eye of Taurus, the Hyades made the face, and in my head they became one object. Then I discovered that Aldebaran has nothing to do with the Hyades. I remember going outside afterward and looking again, half expecting the deception to become obvious now that I knew. It didn't. Aldebaran still looked completely at home among the other stars . The difference is hidden in the one dimension our eyes judge poorly when we look into space — depth. Aldebaran is about 65 light-years away, while the Hyades are roughly 150 light-years distant. The orange eye of Taurus is a foreground star that happens to lie almost exactly along our line of sight toward the Hyades. This fact exposes one of the most convincing tricks in stargazing. The night sky looks flat, and our brains are extremely willing to believe it. But it has incredible depth — and when you can see parts of the night sky in 3D, that's when you begin to appreciate that you're not looking at a flat map. Instead, you begin to see our cosmic neighborhood as it really is. By appreciating depth, you learn its geography. What's happening and when to look Aldebaran, the brightest star in the constellation of Taurus. (Image credit: Christophe Lehenaff via Getty Images) Taurus is now easy to find from the Northern Hemisphere during the evening. Once it's dark, look east for a small, tight knot of stars — the Pleiades open cluster (M45) — and then look nearby for a much larger V-shaped arrangement. That V is the Hyades, with unmistakably orange Aldebaran apparently sitting on one arm. Aldebaran's name is derived from the Arabic Al Dabarān, meaning "the follower," because it appears to trail the Pleiades across the night sky. The Hyades is a real physical group of stars — an open cluster — that formed together and moves through our galaxy together. About 153 light-years away, the Hyades is the nearest open star cluster to Earth. The name means "the rainmakers" because their rising and setting times in the ancient Greek sky coincided with wet weather. The stars in the Hyades are of a similar age — and mostly sun-like stars, or similar — so astronomers can tell that they all formed together in the same nebula . Orange-red star Aldebaran — the 14th-brightest star in the night sky — is the interloper, sitting less than half as far away from the sun . If you could somehow view the neighborhood from another part of the Milky Way , the familiar arrangement would fall apart. Aldebaran would no longer sit conveniently in the bull's face, and Taurus itself would stop looking like a bull. Constellations aren't objects in the same sense as a planet or star cluster. science.title: Could an ancient solar eclipse rewrite Egyptian history?
science.description: null The solar system is a clock that can be run in both directions. On Aug. 2, 2027, that clock will bring the moon's dark central shadow — a path of totality — back to Egypt. A t otal solar eclipse will sweep across the country , passing directly over Luxor and plunging some of ancient Egypt's greatest surviving monuments into darkness. Totality will begin in Luxor at approximately 1:02 p.m. EEST and last 6 minutes 22 seconds, according to Time and Date . We know when it will happen because we can calculate the motions of Earth and the moon centuries in advance. But run the same celestial clock backward and eclipses become one of nature's most precise timestamps. Astronomers can reconstruct where the moon's shadow fell thousands of years ago, even when nobody left a record of it. When an ancient text reliably describes an eclipse, it can anchor a moment in history to a specific place and time. Did an eclipse rewrite the Pyramid Age? Pharaoh Shepseskaf's huge rectangular tomb at South Saqqara (Image credit: Jon Bodsworth - www.egyptarchive.co.uk) We know from astronomical calculations that eclipses crossed Egypt long before anyone left an identifiable written record of one. On April 1, 2471 B.C., a total solar eclipse swept across northern Egypt during the age of the great pyramid builders. In research published in 2025, archaeoastronomer Giulio Magli at the Polytechnic University of Milan proposed that the eclipse may help explain why Pharaoh Shepseskaf broke with tradition and built a huge rectangular tomb at South Saqqara instead of a pyramid. It's a tantalizing hypothesis, but no surviving Egyptian text records the eclipse. Astronomers can calculate that an eclipse happened, but using it as a historical timestamp requires evidence that someone actually saw it and recorded it. That's where an eclipse almost 1,300 years later becomes particularly intriguing. Is the oldest recorded eclipse hidden in the Bible? Researchers have proposed that an annular eclipse occurred over Canaan on Oct. 30, 1207 BC, and may be described in the Bible. This image was captured during an annular solar eclipse from Redding, California on May 20, 2012. (Image credit: Paul Souders via Getty Images) A passage in the Old Testament book of Joshua describes the sun and moon as if they stopped in the sky. And the sun stood still, and the moon stopped, until the nation took vengeance on their enemies." Ancient Gibeon is about six miles (10 kilometers) northwest of Jerusalem. In research published in 2017, researchers Colin Humphreys and Graeme Waddington at Cambridge University in the U.K. claimed it could refer to an annular solar eclipse on Oct. 30, 1207 B.C. science.title: Russia is developing a nuclear space weapon, US intelligence report finds
science.description: null Last month, the U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) released a chilling and info-packed report judging the scope and breadth of threats posed by the nation's adversaries in space. The new report focuses on China , Russia and the emerging space powers of Iran and North Korea. It looks at what's happening in Earth orbit and beyond, including cislunar space, the region between our planet and the moon . The report — the 2026 edition of "Challenges to Security in Space" — is the third iteration of the DIA's unclassified intelligence assessment on space-related challenges and threats to U.S. national security, as well as the extent to which space is treated internationally as a warfighting domain . Information within the report, which you can read here , is current as of July 2026. DIA's mission is to provide intelligence on foreign militaries to help prevent wars, and win the ones that are fought. Up-front finding The report's up-front finding is that China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea are developing, testing, deploying and using space capabilities "in a way that threatens the security of all space systems and their associated space benefits." Indeed, China and Russia are developing "a formidable spectrum" of offensive capabilities to degrade or destroy space services of other countries, from kinetic destruction to sophisticated jamming and cyber operations. The DIA report also notes that "the production of cheaper, smaller, and simpler satellites , which are faster to develop and deploy, along with the expansion of commercially available launch services, are driving the rapid integration of commercial space alternatives to support national security." While space commercialization is making previously government-centered space services widely available to interested parties, the DIA report adds, that availability also includes state and non-state actors with malign interests. There are a range of threats to space-based services, both commercial and military. Some are reversible, while others are not. (Image credit: DIA) Counterspace worries A major item dealt with by the DIA is "counterspace" — and it's not the kind that you'll find in your kitchen. Counterspace operations can be either offensive or defensive. They can be used on purpose to reversibly or irreversibly deny, disrupt, degrade, damage or destroy a space object or component of a space system. Here are the key elements of counterspace, as identified within the DIA report: Antisatellite (ASAT) missiles are designed to kinetically strike and destroy satellites. ASAT missiles could produce massive amounts of debris that can remain in orbit for decades or even centuries. The Riemann hypothesis was first put forward in 1859 by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann. It proposes an origin for the prime numbers, namely that they follow a certain pattern. The question is one of the Clay Mathematics Institute Millennium Prize Problems, which will award a $1 million prize for an accepted solution. Read more OpenAI has dumped 722 maths papers – now it must clean up the mess Levent Alpöge at Anthropic published a statement today claiming to have solved the problem with the aid of Anthropic’s Claude AI. Advertisement “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann hypothesis,” writes Alpöge. “It is natural to feel that this is an end, in my case a loss of a principal guiding light, but what I saw during the course of progress so amazed me that I believe it is one dawn across science of something far greater.” In August, Anthropic announced previous work on the Riemann hypothesis , but that stopped short of a full proof. Alpöge hasn’t published a human-readable version of the proof, saying it would be “obviously inappropriate to attempt to post some massive unreadable travesty of ‘slop'”, though he says an unpublished version ran to more than 250,000 pages. Instead, Alpöge has released a version of the proof written in Lean, a computer code mathematicians use to mechanically verify proofs as a series of logical steps in a process called formalisation. science.title: ISS astronauts look down on the snow-capped Himalayas | Space photo of the day for Nov. 20, 2026
science.description: null A snapshot of the Himalayas captured from aboard the ISS. (Image credit: CSA/Joshua Kutryk) The Himalayas tower below the clouds, capped in icy snow in new snapshots captured from aboard the International Space Station . What is it? Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk was looking out one of the windows aboard the space station when the most incredible view came into focus — and thankfully he had a camera handy and was able to capture these striking scenes of the Himalayas from space. Above the mountain range, fluffy clouds hang in the atmosphere. Below, the expansive Himalayas are covered in bright snow and ice, which looks somehow both white and blue at the same time as the bright sunlight streaks across the breathtaking expanse. This frosty winter scene showcases the mountain range from orbit, from about 250 miles (400 kilometers) above Earth's surface. But even from this distance, the magnitude of this mountain range is palpable. The Himalayas stretch across five different countries including Nepal, India, China, Bhutan and Pakistan. And the Himalayas include some of the highest mountain peaks on planet Earth, including Mount Everest. Himalayas 🗻 https://t.co/IzGzu20H4Q November 17, 2026 Why is it incredible? From orbit around Earth, you might expect even the largest landmarks on our planet to appear miniscule. But somehow, in these photographs snapped by Kutryk during NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 mission , even from hundreds of miles above our planet you can really see and feel the immense scale of this mammoth mountain range. It's unclear exactly where above the mountain range these photographs were taken, but it is always amazing to think that within these sweeping landscapes are people living their lives, likely unaware that an astronaut is taking in the beauty of their home. Perhaps somewhere hidden under the clouds in one of Kutryk's photographs are hikers climbing up the side of Mt. Everest, completing their own bucket list adventure as the astronauts watching from above complete theirs.
